Conflict: The In-Service Agent recommends impact-resistant virgin polymer to ensure durability and prevent premature obsolescence, whereas the Material and Design Agent recommends a recycled polypropylene monomaterial structure which has lower impact resistance and mechanical durability.
Agents Involved: In-Service Agent; Material and Design Agent
Rationale: To balance durability and recycled content, we select the recycled polypropylene monomaterial structure but specify structural ribbing to meet durability requirements without compromising recyclability.

Conflict: The In-Service Agent recommends threaded metal fasteners with brass inserts for robust repairability, whereas the Manufacture Agent rejects this due to increased assembly complexity and the Circularity Agent prefers simple snap-fits and standard screws to avoid multi-material contamination.
Agents Involved: In-Service Agent; Manufacture Agent; Circularity Agent
Rationale: Reversible mechanical fasteners avoid chemical adhesives and metal inserts, ensuring ease of disassembly for repair and clean material separation for recycling.

Conflict: The In-Service Agent recommends a high-efficiency brushless DC motor to maximize energy efficiency, whereas the Manufacture Agent recommends a magnet-free synchronous reluctance motor to avoid the high environmental footprint of rare-earth mining.
Decision: High-efficiency brushless DC motor with modular, extractable magnets
Rationale: This choice delivers high in-service energy efficiency and lifetime while using a modular design with non-glued, extractable magnets to facilitate recycling of critical raw materials.

Conflict: The In-Service Agent recommends active fan cooling with replaceable dust filters to maintain operating reliability, whereas the Circularity Agent rejects this due to the generation of consumable filter waste at end-of-life.
Decision: Passive cooling via integrated aluminum heat sinks
Rationale: Passive heat sinks with dry thermal pads eliminate the need for consumable filters and active fan components, reducing waste while providing reliable cooling.

Conflict: The In-Service and Circularity Agents recommend a fully modular architecture with separable functional cassettes to maximize repairability, whereas the Manufacture Agent recommends a monolithic integrated design to minimize manufacturing energy and waste.
Agents Involved: In-Service Agent; Manufacture Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Modular architecture with standardized, separable functional blocks
Rationale: A modular architecture is selected because ease of repair and refurbishment are key parameters under ESPR Annex I to prevent premature obsolescence, overriding manufacturing simplicity.

Conflict: The In-Service Agent recommends a removable and standardized lithium-ion battery pack to ensure functional performance and repairability, whereas the Circularity and Manufacture Agents recommend a corded AC power supply to eliminate battery manufacturing impacts and hazardous waste.
Agents Involved: In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent; Manufacture Agent
Decision: Removable and standardized lithium-ion battery pack
Rationale: A removable and standardized battery pack is selected to ensure functional performance and mobility while addressing the primary failure point of cordless vacuums through easy battery replacement.
